Permutation null for banded-ridge prediction accuracy

Source: R/banded_ridge_weights.R
banded_ridge_null.Rd

Tests the held-out accuracy of every response against a null in which the predicted series is shifted in time against the observed one. Shifting keeps the autocorrelation of both series, which a row shuffle would destroy, so the null is appropriate for continuous time series. No model is refit.

Usage

banded_ridge_null(
  model,
  result,
  n_perm = 1000L,
  metric = c("correlation", "r2"),
  strategy = c("circular_shift", "block_shuffle"),
  block_size = NULL,
  min_shift = 1L,
  seed = 1L
)

Arguments

model

A `banded_ridge_model` built with `return_predictions = TRUE`.

result

The result of `run_banded_ridge(model)`.

n_perm

Number of permutations.

metric

`"correlation"` (default) or `"r2"`.

strategy

`"circular_shift"` (default) or `"block_shuffle"`.

block_size

Block length for `"block_shuffle"`; defaults to `floor(sqrt(n))`.

min_shift

Smallest circular shift, in rows. Set it beyond the autocorrelation length of the data.

seed

Integer seed; the same permutations are applied to every response.

Value

A data frame with one row per response: `voxel_index`, the observed `statistic`, the permutation `p_value` (one-sided, observed value counted in the null), and `z`, the statistic standardized by the null.

Details

The null addresses the full model's accuracy. It does not test a band's unique contribution: shifting the predictions of the full and reduced models together leaves their difference near zero by construction.

See also

[run_banded_ridge()]
